idiom_name: delegating facade class (subsystem headers hidden in the .cpp)
implementation_notes: Classic C++ form: a class whose member functions delegate to subsystem objects it owns or receives; include the subsystem headers only in the .cpp (or apply pimpl when the facade is public ABI) so clients do not recompile against the subsystem. The alternative realization is a namespace of free functions: anything implementable through the public interface should be a non-member per C++ Coding Standards' 'prefer nonmember, nonfriends', and std::filesystem is the standard-library precedent of a namespace facade over platform APIs. Keep the class when the facade must be passed around, hold configuration or be substituted polymorphically; prefer the free-function namespace when it is a stateless set of operations.
pitfalls: Subsystem headers dragged into the facade's public header recreate the compile-time coupling the facade is supposed to cut; use pimpl or keep members in the .cpp.
Returning subsystem types (or taking them as parameters) ties clients to the internals anyway; return facade-owned value types.
A facade class that is also the subsystem's owner must state ownership in the type (unique_ptr members) instead of leaking raw pointers.

variants.name: Namespace of free functions
variants.idiom_name: namespace-scoped free functions over the subsystem
variants.implementation_notes: The facade is a namespace, not a class: calls read f(x) instead of x.f(), no object needs to exist, and the API can be extended without touching a class. This is the shape std::filesystem uses for its operations and the reason the C++ Coding Standards say to prefer non-member functions when they can be implemented through the public interface. Choose it when the facade is stateless and value-based; if configuration or polymorphism enters, switch to the class variant rather than accumulating function parameters.
pitfalls: Header-only free-function facades change every call site's syntax relative to the class form; mixing both styles in one library is confusing.
Free functions cannot carry configuration; parameters or a separate options struct grow unboundedly unless the API is designed around tasks.
